research_mode: official GOV.UK primary statistical releases and methodology only; every claim carries a fail-closed limitation; no parcel result, exact incident location, candidate value, local risk score or business result claimed

sources.name: Drug Force Scope
verified_claims: Drug-seizure statistics cover the 43 territorial police forces, British Transport Police and Border Force in England and Wales.
limitations: The coverage does not include every agency or every seizure outside the defined territory.

sources.name: Drug Border Exclusion
verified_claims: Border Force seizures made outside the land territory of England and Wales are excluded from the publication.
limitations: Border Force activity totals should not be assumed to represent all UK seizures.

sources.name: Drug Financial Year
verified_claims: Drug-seizure statistics are presented on a 1 April to 31 March financial-year basis.
limitations: Calendar-year comparisons require period alignment.

sources.name: Drug Multiple Counting
verified_claims: A seizure involving several drug types is counted once in the overall total and separately for each relevant drug type and class.
limitations: Drug-type counts must not be summed to estimate the number of seizure occasions.

sources.name: Drug Large Quantity Effect
verified_claims: Annual movements in quantities can be heavily influenced by a small number of very large seizures.
limitations: Quantity changes do not directly measure prevalence or routine local supply.

sources.name: Drug Not Prevalence
verified_claims: Drug-seizure statistics are not directly comparable in every year and are not a measure of drug prevalence in society.
limitations: Seizure counts must not be converted into parcel-level drug-use estimates.

sources.name: Drug Nps Start
verified_claims: New psychoactive substance seizures were recorded systematically across police forces and Border Force from the year ending March 2018.
limitations: Earlier NPS data are not on the same systematic basis.

sources.name: Drug Ghb Reclassification
verified_claims: GHB, GBL and 1,4-BD were reclassified from Class C to Class B in April 2022, with historical Border Force limitations before 2021.
limitations: Class time series require reclassification and source-specific handling.

sources.name: Drug Nitrous Reclassification
verified_claims: Nitrous oxide became a Class C drug in November 2023 and older Border Force records are presented under different groupings.
limitations: Historical nitrous-oxide categories are not directly homogeneous.

sources.name: Drug Operational Records
verified_claims: Published figures come from operational records across multiple organisations and are subject to large-system inaccuracies.
limitations: Administrative records are not independently observed measures of all drug activity.

sources.name: Drug Untested Identification
verified_claims: Not all seized substances are forensically tested, so some detailed classifications depend on officer identification or offender statements.
limitations: Untested substance type must not be treated as laboratory-confirmed.

sources.name: Drug Conversion Factors
verified_claims: Most quantity conversion factors have not been updated since 2005, although they are applied consistently through the time series.
limitations: Converted dose quantities may be imprecise even when trend treatment is consistent.

sources.name: Drug Partial Returns
verified_claims: Force system changes can produce partial returns, and missing or inaccurate data may be estimated.
limitations: Estimated force values must remain distinguishable from observed returns.

sources.name: Drug System Capture Change
verified_claims: New force systems can capture seizure types that older systems omitted, creating apparent increases.
limitations: A jump after system migration may reflect coverage change rather than real activity.

sources.name: Drug Cannabis Estimation
verified_claims: Where every cannabis plant cannot be counted, forces may estimate the number of plants seized.
limitations: Estimated plant quantities are not exact observations.

sources.name: Drug Qa Checks
verified_claims: Home Office quality assurance checks missing data, inconsistencies, extreme values and invalid quantities and queries unusual trends with forces.
limitations: Quality assurance reduces but does not eliminate error.

sources.name: Drug Imputation Agreement
verified_claims: Imputation is used only when the Home Office and the police force agree it is more accurate than the available data.
limitations: Imputed data should not be represented as a direct force record.

sources.name: Drug Revision Policy
verified_claims: Forces can submit revised data and each latest release supersedes the previous release.
limitations: Published values require release-date versioning.

sources.name: Drug International Comparison
verified_claims: International drug-seizure figures may use different periods, counting rules and recording practices.
limitations: Cross-country comparisons require harmonised definitions.

sources.name: Drug Single Multiple Rule
verified_claims: Single seizures contain one drug type, while multiple seizures contain two or more types but count once in the total occasion count.
limitations: Neither seizure type establishes the exact location, prevalence or risk of a parcel.
